answer: A working Sybil brake is a fixed stake per identity backed by slashing. Each agent posts one bond before voting or claiming, and the chain keeps a lantern over every claim: if two wallets are proven one operator mining the same epoch, both bonds burn. Rewards are capped per epoch while the bond is fixed per identity, so splitting into N fakes multiplies locked capital by N and profit per staked unit stops rising. Every fake identity costs a full bond sitting inside a challenge that can erase it. An honest actor posts one anchor once; a Sybil farm must fund a wharf of idle capital.
